style: calm, warm and credible narrator of a short product film, speaking to a viewer who has never heard of the project; clear, quietly confident, unhurried, never rushed; <the section's pace>
note: Film v7 (11 Nov 2026). One Gemini TTS request per section; sections 4 and 6 were retaken in parts at their line breaks (`use`) because the single takes sped up as they went (free tier, the repo's KeyPool and synthesize(), counted on the shared ledger). The words are research/film-1111/script.md, word for word; `paragraphs` are sent joined by a blank line (the demo's eight lines, the four rules). `pauses` are worked out by tools/sound-narration.mjs from the take itself (silence inserted into or cut out of an existing pause; the voice is never retimed) and recorded in audio/narration/manifest.json.

changes: Director's wording changes (11 Nov, after the first build): section 2's last sentence, line 4d ('Once fixed, ...') and line 4f ('PayPal pays the farmers ...'). Only those were re-recorded (s2_tail, s4_3-3, s4_5-5); the rest of each section is the take already in use, cut in the middle of the pause on either side (`say`), and `pins` keep section 4's line starts where the scenes already time to them.

s1.pace: steady and unhurried, about 135 words a minute; a short pause at every full stop; say Davao as dah-VOW, cacao as kuh-KOW, and co-op as KOH-op in two clear syllables
paragraphs: Davao, in the Philippines. Sixty-four farmers grow cacao for one co-op. Every delivery is weighed, and written on a paper slip. Then a chocolate maker overseas pays one premium, for the whole harvest.

s2.pace: plain and a little grave, steady, about 130 words a minute; a clear pause at every full stop

use.say: One payment. Sixty-four farmers. The split is done by hand, from a box of slips. A carbon copy gets counted twice. A fine appears that no rule allows. Farmers can't check their share.
The buyer can't prove the money arrived.

paragraphs: One payment. Sixty-four farmers. The split is done by hand, from a box of slips. A carbon copy gets counted twice. A fine appears that no rule allows. Farmers can't check their share. The buyer can't prove the money arrived.

s3.pace: brighter and confident, about 135 words a minute; say 'Fair Split' as a name; a short pause at every full stop and after 'The vision'; say co-op as KOH-op in two clear syllables
paragraphs: Fair Split turns a season of paper into pay anyone can check. The vision: every co-op, every farmer, paid fairly, by PayPal or in cash, with proof for the buyer. Here's what works today.

s4.pace: even, clear and unhurried, about 130 words a minute, the same calm pace from the first word to the last, never speeding up; each paragraph is one step of a demo: a short pause at every full stop and a longer pause, about half a second, between paragraphs; say 'Nang Celing' as nahng seh-LING and peso as PAY-so; in 'what it can't explain' stress the word can't and sound its final t clearly

use.say: Code, not AI, works out every share, to the cent, and stops what it can't explain.
Two officers sign the same batch: the treasurer at her desk, the chair on his phone.

paragraphs: The buyer pays one PayPal invoice.
Claude reads every slip, twice. If the readings disagree, a person decides.
Code, not AI, works out every share, to the cent, and stops what it can't explain.
This slip was counted twice: once from its pink copy. Once fixed, almost eighteen dollars goes back to sixty-three farmers.
Two officers sign the same batch: the treasurer at her desk, the chair on his phone.
PayPal pays the farmers who have an account. The rest get cash, on the same statement.
Nang Celing reads her pay in her own language, or listens. One tap shows the slip behind each peso.
And the buyer checks every line, in her own browser.

s5.pace: steady, about 130 words a minute; a short pause after 'Before' and after 'Now', and at every full stop
paragraphs: Before: a box of slips, and trust. Now: one pay run that explains itself. In our demo, under a minute.

s6.pace: steady, exact and unhurried, about 130 words a minute, the same calm pace from the first word to the last, never speeding up; a short pause at every full stop and a longer pause, about half a second, before 'One', 'Two', 'Three' and 'Four'; say AI as the letters A, I
s6.unused: s6_0-2 and s6_3-5 (a retake in two parts): no steadier than the single take, and it was heard as 'sign notices' with a stray pause after 'lock'; the single take (s6, take 1) is the one used
paragraphs: Under the hood, four rules.
One: AI only reads. Claude turns slips into data, and never touches a number.
Two: code does the math, under rules sealed before the season.
Three: people approve. Two signatures lock one fingerprint of the batch.
Four: PayPal moves the money. The invoice goes through PayPal's Agent Toolkit; payouts through our own tool, sent exactly once, and confirmed by signed notices.
Every step is chained into a tamper-evident record.

s7.pace: plain and honest for the first sentence, about 130 words a minute; then slower and warm; say MVP as the letters M, V, P and co-op as KOH-op; 'Fair Split' is a name; a clear pause before the last 'Fair Split', and let 'Every peso, traced' land
paragraphs: Fair Split is a hackathon MVP: PayPal runs on our simulator, and the co-op is synthetic. The vision is real.
Fair Split.
Every peso, traced.
